name: KLASH
summary: A historical low-frequency axion-search concept using the large-volume KLOE magnet.
detection_principle: A large cryogenic resonant cavity accumulates axion-conversion power in a moderate magnetic field and reads out weak microwaves.

sites.name: INFN Frascati, proposed location in the former KLOE magnet
sites.location: INFN Frascati, proposed location in the former KLOE magnet

status.label: Public proposal / conceptual design
status.evidence: 2019 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

collaboration.name: KLASH Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: The conceptual report evaluates sensitivity and feasibility; its construction timescale was a projection at the time, not evidence of completion.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
